verdict.rationale: Visa Intelligent Commerce documents first-party rails for agent-initiated purchases. These include agent-specific network tokens, passkey-authenticated purchase-intent mandates, and credential retrieval scoped to a named merchant and amount. Its Trusted Agent Protocol lets merchants verify agents and receive checkout data, and an MCP server/agent toolkit can create payment links. So an assistant can complete a purchase at a Visa-accepting merchant. However, the evidence never documents a merchant-facing way to list or sell products directly inside named chat surfaces. ChatGPT appears only in a community comment reacting to news, and the product is flagged as still 'in the process of development and deployment.' Missing for 10: documented integrations with ChatGPT/Claude/Gemini/Copilot checkout surfaces, merchant catalog/product exposure to assistants, production availability, and independent hands-on corroboration.
